result.title: Benchmarking uncertainty quantification for engineering regression under graded distribution shift
result.summary: Machine learning models in engineering are often used beyond their training conditions, where reliable uncertainty quantification (UQ) matters most. Existing comparisons of regression UQ methods rely on random splits, which assess calibration only in distribution. We introduce a three-rung shift ladder (in distribution, soft shift and hard shift) built along physically meaningful shift variables, and evaluate 12 methods from five families on seven public engineering datasets: five extrapolation settings, an unseen turbofan fault mode and a winter air-quality sensor deployment. All tuning uses source data only. In distribution, conformal methods cover at least 0.946 of test points on every dataset. Under hard shift, mean coverage falls to 0.40-0.75 across the 11 methods that always return an interval, and no systematic difference in method ranks is detected (Friedman p = 0.63). Weighted conformalised quantile regression stays near nominal on the points it answers, but abstains on 85\% of hard-shift points on average and covers only 0.67 of the few Concrete points it answers. Source-validation gains predict improvement in distribution and under soft shift, but not under hard shift (Spearman's rho = 0.04). Engineering evaluations should split calibration data by deployment unit, report subgroup coverage and sharpness, and treat abstention as an explicit operational outcome.

AI.brief_summary: 论文沿具物理意义的偏移变量搭建「同分布—软偏移—硬偏移」三级阶梯，在七个工程回归数据集上评测五个家族共 12 种不确定性量化方法的覆盖率、锐度与弃权行为，并指出基于源数据的验证收益在硬偏移下失效。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把弃权作为显式运行结果、按部署单元分组报告覆盖率与锐度的做法，可能为考察 LVR 中 STOP/弃权决策在分布偏移下的可靠性、置信标定与成本提供可供核查的评价视角。
